headline: Public transcriptomic datasets and machine learning nominate candidate disease biomarkers
label: Machine Learning Transcriptomic Biomarker Discovery
summary: Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomics with machine learning nominate candidate biomarkers and targets across diverse diseases.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational prioritization of candidate molecular targets from public or multi-omics data, followed in some items by limited experimental validation. Several papers apply limma, WGCNA, PPI network analysis, and machine-learning feature selection to GEO transcriptomes, nominating hub genes such as THY1 in osteoarthritis, DNM1L in OA subtypes, JUN and MYC in acetylation-related OA, CCL5, FOXC1, and LTF in diabetic kidney disease, and five ferroptosis/cuproptosis-linked genes in ulcerative colitis. Single-cell analysis is added in the diabetic foot ulcer, vascular calcification, and ulcerative colitis studies to resolve cell-type-specific dysregulation. Other items extend the approach to network pharmacology and metabolomics for traditional formulations, and to LC-MS-guided compound identification. What is new is mainly the combination of bulk, single-cell, and metabolomic evidence in candidate prioritization, though these items report hypothesis-generating associations rather than predictive models.
